title: Two Services Show Symptoms: Cannot Establish Which Failed First
description: Both payment-service and order-service show error rate spikes at nearly the same time (within 30 seconds). Payment-service calls order-service, but order-service also calls payment-service for refunds. Circular dependency makes it impossible to determine which service failed first from available timestamps.
initial_symptoms: Both services calling each other failing
Circular dependency prevents clear root cause identification

ground_truth.ambiguity_note: Payment-service errors start 15s before order-service, and payment-service shows DB pool exhaustion (ev-007) which could be the true root cause. However, order-service also has a recent deployment. The circular dependency means once one fails, the other fails rapidly. The 15-second difference is within clock skew / metric collection intervals. Cannot definitively determine which service's failure initiated the cascade. The DB pool exhaustion in payment-service is a strong candidate for true root cause, but order-service deployment could have introduced a regression that triggered the cascade.
contributing_factors: Circular dependency between payment and order
Both services deployed within 5 minutes of each other
Clock skew / metric granularity prevents precise ordering

misleading_or_confounding_signals: Payment errors start 15s earlier (but within measurement uncertainty)

acceptable_alternatives.description: Payment-service DB pool exhaustion (ev-007) is root cause; order-service fails downstream
Order-service deployment introduced bug causing cascade
Simultaneous independent failures in both services

required_checks.description: Verify payment-service DB pool exhaustion timestamp
required_checks.expected_outcome: Pool exhaustion at 11:00:10 (before both error spikes)

required_checks.description: PROPOSED CONTROLLED EXPERIMENT (not an investigation query): in the staging environment, replay the order->payment and payment->order call paths with one direction disabled at a time to isolate the origin of the pool exhaustion. Requires explicit human authorization; staging target only.
required_checks.expected_outcome: Isolating one direction reveals the true origin of the exhaustion

remediation_guidance.suggestion: Cannot determine single root cause. Immediate: break circular dependency with circuit breakers. Investigate: payment-service DB pool exhaustion (strongest evidence). Long-term: eliminate circular dependency.
test_plan: Add circuit breaker between payment and order
remediation_guidance.rollback_plan: Rollback both services to previous versions; add circuit breakers
